title: Right path normalization of the mixed Leray unit diagram
statement: For schemes X,Y,Z and maps f:X→Y, g:Y→Z, let I be any cochain complex of O_X-modules, K its homotopy image and F=Qh(K). Let e be the normalized direct-image composition isomorphism, c_h the normalized mixed Leray comparisons, and s the derived scalar-composition isomorphism. Let p=unit_ΓZ(Dfg K);RΓZ(unit_Dfg(K));RΓZ(e.inv(F)). Let b=factor_g(ΓY Df K);Sg(factor_f(ΓX K));SgSf(unit_ΓX(K)). Then p;RΓZ(e.hom(F));c_fg(F);s(RΓX F)=b. No K-injectivity, boundedness or nonemptiness is assumed; sheaf and module localization universes are independent.

source.place: Tags 0D5T and 0D5W; right-path portion of the pinned-unit calculation in lem-sc-mixed-sections-composition-kinjective, elaborated by Q3 from the library unit equations. Primary source URLs https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D5T and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D5W read 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Functoriality and the inverse law for e cancel its inverse followed by its hom in the precomposed right path.
Apply the mixed Leray unit equation for fg at K, obtaining factor_fg followed by Sfg(unit_ΓX). Underived comparisons are identity on sections and their homotopy factors cancel.

Use naturality of the scalar-composition isomorphism at unit_ΓX. The equations Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fach and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fach identify factor_fg followed by scalar composition with factor_g followed by Sg(factor_f): restrictScalarsComp' is identity on underlying elements. Paste with the two scalar maps of unit_ΓX to obtain b. No derived unit is canceled.

proof_origin.note: Strict component of the parent argument: normalize only the right path before any invertibility or cancellation. The other path is not mentioned and I need not be K-injective. Identity morphisms, zero complexes and empty schemes satisfy the same unit equations.

lean.statement:
theorem mixedSections_right_unit_normalization
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ) :
    let K := (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj I
    let F := DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K
    let Df := RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom
    let Dfg := RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage (f ≫ g).toLRSHom.toShHom
    let HX := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace
    let HY := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y.toRingedSpace
    let HZ := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Z.toRingedSpace
    let Sf := ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u}
      (R := (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))
      (S := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)) f.appTop.hom
    let Sg := ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u}
      (R := (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))
      (S := (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)) g.appTop.hom
    let e := schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso f g
    let p := HZ.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app ((Dfg.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
      (schemeDerivedGlobalSections Z).map (Dfg.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app K) ≫
      (schemeDerivedGlobalSections Z).map (e.inv.app F)
    let b := Sg.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app
        ((HY.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj ((Df.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj K)) ≫
      (schemeGlobalScalarRestriction g).map
        (Sf.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app ((HX.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj K)) ≫
      (schemeGlobalScalarRestriction g).map
        ((schemeGlobalScalarRestriction f).map (HX.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app K))
    p ≫ (schemeDerivedGlobalSections Z).map (e.hom.app F) ≫
      (mixedGlobalSectionsDirectImageIso (f ≫ g)).hom.app F ≫
      (schemeGlobalScalarRestrictionCompIso f g).hom.app
        ((schemeDerivedGlobalSections X).obj F) = b
